Opening a world of learning and opportunity​​​​​​​
Motivated, Independent, Resilient, Responsible, Open-minded, Respectful
Welcome to
Vigo Primary School
We are proud of our happy and friendly school in which staff, governors, children and parents work hard to provide the best possible start to school life. All members of our school community work to fulfil our Vision Statement and to develop our ‘MIRROR’ learning values in our children. We are proud of how everyone works together to reinforce and implement the aims of our school. A school will only achieve its full potential if we all work together, teaching the importance of the experience of school, to help our children value education and learning. At Vigo Primary School we encourage each child’s sense of self-worth and develop the child’s capacity to live as an independent, self-motivated person who respects and values themselves and all others.

Goodbye Year 6 For lots of you, we have watched you grow from tiny little Year Rs into mature young people who are so ready for their next step. These photos capture some of the ways the children celebrated their final day at school today. We wish you all the luck in the world for your next adventure
Winchester University Exhibition! We are also collaborating with Hampshire County Council's 'Climate Unity Programme' and the music department, which generously provided us with the musical instruments for this project. Our Year 2 classes have been working together to transform these instruments into a tribute to our lovely choir, highlighting the importance of the circular economy. It looks fantastic! The exhibition is open until July 22 at the Winchester University Art Gallery. It even includes a QR Code which automatically plays a wonderful recording of our incredible choir so please visit if you have the chance.
Art at the Station! Message from Mrs Marta... In collaboration with the Hampshire Art Society, our Year 3 students created fantastic collages as a tribute to the Mexican artist "Frida Kahlo". Twelve art pieces have been chosen and exhibited in the waiting rooms at Andover train station. Frida's exhibition at the TATE Gallery in London is a highlight of the summer art events, and this is our small contribution to the "Making of the Icon" exhibition. If you're traveling by train this summer, I encourage you to stop by and see our school's work on displayit's a wonderful feeling to see our efforts recognised!
There's something in our eyes Check out these wonderful pictures of our incredible Year 6 children who attended their graduation ceremony @ The Lights Andover We are so proud of everything they have achieved during their time at Vigo and wish them the happiest final week with us
Check out our incredible Country Dancers creating smiles in the community
Special Shout out Following an unprecedented week of challenging temperatures, we would like to take this opportunity to thank our incredible staff team who have worked tirelessly this week in extremely challenging conditions to provide a safe and happy space for the children. Mrs Dance and our wonderful Friends Of Vigo Primary School treated the staff team to an ice cream from the ice cream van after school - this was really appreciated by the staff team and was a lovely gesture of grattitude. We'd like to also thank our wonderful parent/carer community who have shown so much kindness, empathy and understanding throughout the week - this does not go unnoticed we understand that this week has required enormous flexibility and we really appreciate the collaborative approach to supporting the children's safety and well-being. And finally...the most important thank you to our incredible children. Their resilience and open mindedness never ceases to amaze us. It's been a week of different classrooms and different timings but as usual the children have taken it all in their stride. REMINDER Tomorrow (Friday 26th June) the school is open as usual. Due to the continuing high temperatures parents/carers have the option for an early collection. Key Stage 1: 1:10pm Key Stage 2: 1:20pm We ask that you complete the GoogleForm which has been sent out earlier today by the office team to make us aware of your intention to collect early.

Breakfast Club and After School Childcare
Vigo Primary School offers an in-house breakfast club from 7:45am in the morning. We have links with The Scot Centre (Youth Options), which offer after-school childcare. Please see below for more information about before and after childcare.
Vigo Primary School Breakfast Club
Vigo Primary School Breakfast Club is an in-house, pre-booked childcare club operating daily during term time (excluding INSET days). Children are provided with a choice of toast, cereal and juice and are given the opportunity to socialise with their peers, carry out quiet activities such as colouring/drawing and play games inside and outside (weather permitting). We accept children from all year groups (R to 6) and all VPS staff are appropriately trained.
The drop-off point for the club is the school office. Please queue outside the main entrance and a member of the VPS Breakfast Club team will open the external door to let you through at the following times:
Please note, staff will open the gates at these times only, they will not wait by the door, you will need to arrive promptly for the times stated above and if you arrive later than your desired time slot please queue until the next opening time.
Breakfast Club registration forms can be downloaded from our website or requested at the school office. There is an initial, one-off registration fee of £2.50 for every child attending the club. This must be paid via Scopay at the point of registering your child and before any booked sessions take place.
If you require assistance with logging on to your child’s Scopay account, please contact Mr Christmas in the school office.
We accept child care/employers' vouchers as a method of payment, as well as the government tax-free childcare scheme. If you are registered with a childcare voucher scheme, please ensure you include these details on the registration form to enable us to update our records.
If you would like to register and book your child in to sessions for VPS Breakfast Club, please complete the registration form and email it to adminoffice@vigo.hants.sch.uk
1st Entry Time – 7:45am
2nd Entry Time – 8:00am
3rd Entry Time – 8:15am
The Scott Centre - After-School Childcare
At Vigo Primary School we regularly review the demand for wrap-around and after-school childcare. Currently, we do have links with The Scott Centre after-school childcare club in Andover, run by Youth Options. A mini-bus is in operation from the school to their centre at Mead Hedges, Andover, SP10 2LB every day during term time.
If you would like to book your child in for after-school childcare with The Scott Centre please contact them directly on T: 01264 332188 or visit their website at https://youthoptions.org.uk/what-we-do/our-centres/scott-centre
360° Sports Coaching - After-School Childcare
360° Sports Coaching after-school childcare club will operate at Vigo Primary School every school day during term time (excludes INSET days) from September 2024. There are a range of activities available at the club, which is split into two sessions:
*Session 1 and 2 combined will be a total cost of £12 per day
All sessions must be booked in advance and paid for directly with the 360° Team. For more information please click on the links below.

Governors are not expected to be involved in the day to day running of the school but take a strategic approach, we have three core functions which are:

At Vigo Primary School we are fortunate in having a governing body with a wide range of skills and experience. We are committed to ensuring that children receive a high quality education which enables them to reach their full potential within a caring school community where they feel valued and safe.
Throughout the year we aim to provide you with updates via the website and look forward to meeting you in school. Thank you for your support.
There is no member of staff at Vigo Primary school who earns over £100k per year.
About Our School

Junior Governors
Welcome to our Junior Governor page.
We are representatives from each year group who meet to discuss current ideas and concerns that the children at Vigo primary school may have. Our intention is to support the children, staff governors and senior leadership team at Vigo to develop our school so that it grows from strength to strength. Pupil voice is important, and we represent this important role within the school by talking to our classmates and meeting with each other weekly, supported by Mr Stott.
This academic year (2024/25) we have achieved:
Meeting with Mrs Johnson, our school's Chair of Governors, to share what we do and what is important to the children at Vigo. We look forward to meeting with her again in this final half-term of the academic year.
Supported the Purple Oak charity by raising money to donate to this valuable local charity which supports our community.
Successfully rebranded our school houses – we established the new names by enabling our classmates to vote; designed the icons to represent each house; communicated the changes to all stakeholders and created two house displays in each school hall. We also created and now use house flags for each house which were displayed on sports day.
What are we currently working on?
We completed our London Trip!
The Junior Governors, along with a few lucky students from across the school, went with Mr Stott, Mrs Dance, Mr Kew, Mrs Johnson (Governor) and Mrs Tucker (Governor). After a long journey on the coach, we arrived and had a tour of Parliament. We saw the history of British democracy and learnt lots about the democratic process. Luckily, we were allowed entry into the House of Lords and saw the golden throne that the king sits on when he visits. After that, we then enjoyed a picnic lunch in the parliament gardens before touring some of London's tourist sites, including 10 Downing Street, Westminster Abbey, Elizabeth Tower and the London Eye. Attached below are some of our pictures from the day.
We will be updating the page regularly to give you an insight into what we have discussed and what we have achieved-so please come back and visit this page when you can.

Meet Our Governors
Marty Johnson, Chair
I have lived near Andover for many years and have three grown up children. I worked at Andover College as both a Lecturer and as an LSA where I supported students helping them to achieve their learning goals. I have also worked at a local village Primary school so I have experience working with learners from Year R to A level.
I joined the GB at Vigo in 2015 as a co-opted governor and became Chair of Governors in 2018 when Julie Bray was appointed Head Teacher. The GB were delighted to welcome Rachel Dance to this role last year. It has been an exciting and rewarding experience to be part of the school over the last few years when it has gone from strength to strength. As a Governing Body we are committed to developing and supporting improvements ensuring every child will achieve their learning potential and enjoy their time at Vigo.
Andrew Murray
I was co-opted as a Governor in December 2019 but I have lived in the area close to Whitchurch since 1997. I am a chartered accountant who has worked within small and medium sized businesses since leaving one of the major accounting practices. My current role is as group finance director for a small group of travel and leisure companies and my responsibilities include all finance, HR and IT areas. I am a trustee of a two charities including Fine Cell Work a charity and social enterprise which enables prisoners to build fulfilling and crime-free lives. I have two grown up children and my knowledge of the education sector is patchy but even at my age I am still willing to learn.
Leah Tucker
I have lived in Andover all my life and have three children, all of whom attended Vigo. I joined the Governing Board in September 2013. I have a Diploma in Early Years and have worked with children since leaving college in 2000. At the present time I am a child minder but before meeting my husband and having my own children, I worked as a nanny. I have a great understanding of Early Years education and I am also trained to Level Four in Safe Guarding. I am a Safe Guarding Governor and Early Years Governor. I am also on the Pay and Curriculum committees at Vigo.
Sophie Salvidge
I am a parent governor with a child at Vigo. I grew up in a village not far from Andover, and I now live in Andover. I work as a Commercial Property and Asset Manager. I am hoping my property, health and safety and budgeting knowledge, as well as offering a parental perspective, will be useful to Vigo and the Board of Governors. I am so pleased to be able to be part of Vigo’s future and its ability to offer all the children a safe environment for education and play
Dr Will Liddell
I was born and brought up just outside Andover and have worked for many years as a GP in the town, including as a school doctor. I retired in 2018, but I still work part-time in family medicine, while running a farming business. I have a PGCE, but my educational experience is in adult education and particularly the training and supervision of doctors. I regard a good primary school education as a key determinant of long-term health and well-being and therefore of enormous importance.
Frances Bernon
I was a Financial Controller for an engineering company and retired during Lockdown when I volunteered as a Math’s tutor for a charity. I taught Keystage 2 maths to pupils from schools in Liverpool and London on line and really enjoyed the experience, finding it very rewarding. Although I have not worked in education, I am hoping my financial and mathematical background will prove useful to the school. I have two grownup boys and believe all children deserve the best education possible and I am excited to be part of Vigo school.
Gold Pravin
I moved to the UK from India in 2019 and have since lived in Andover. I have served across Asia leading Youth and child development programs yielding to UN SDG Goals. I am passionate about child / youth empowerment, agency and advocacy. Currently I work in the FinTech space. I love outdoor adventure activities, and am an avid car and motorbike enthusiast. Passionate about food, cooking and bringing people together through food. I am excited to have been appointed as a co-opted governor. I am eager to use my global exposure, experience and broad cultural curiosity in empowering teachers and children to reach their true potential and being at their best.
Dr Stephen Anning
I am excited to join Vigo Primary School’s governing board as a parent governor. I have a passion for empowering people with technology. My experience includes working with police forces to develop technologies for tackling modern slavery and safeguarding children from exploitation. I also work in the Army Artificial Intelligence Centre as a Reservist to promote the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence across the Army. As an academic, I currently teach master’s students about artificial intelligence in modern society, and my business focusses on tackling online harms. I feel quite energised by being part of the success of Vigo’s children and the school's extraordinary teachers.
Tom Cox
I was appointed as staff governor at Vigo in 2024. I started at the school in 2023, as an LSA, and I am currently working in Year 6 with aspirations to become a teacher and eventually a headteacher. I am proud to serve as a Staff Governor and to represent the views and experiences of colleagues within the school. In this role, I aim to support the school’s strategic direction, contribute to effective governance, and help ensure decisions are made in the best interests of pupils, staff, and the wider school community. A key focus of my work is promoting positive mental health and wellbeing, recognising the importance of a supportive and inclusive environment for both staff and students to thrive.
Anna Bowyer
I joined the board of Governors in January 2026 and am very excited to be part of the incredible team that work and support Vigo in a new capacity. I worked for 5 years at Vigo as a class teacher supporting as the Computing Lead and also as a coach and mentor for staff. I was a primary teacher for 15 years and now teach adults in the military. I live in a village just outside Andover. I look forward to supporting staff, leadership and the community in continuously ensuring Vigo is a vibrant, innovative and creative educational facility where young people thrive and staff are developed.

Welcome from Mrs Dance
Welcome to Vigo Primary School.
We hope you find all the information that you need on our website. If not, please give us a call or email us so that we can answer any questions that you may have.
Vigo is a large three-form entry primary school where our children and teaching team thrive in a friendly, welcoming and nurturing environment.
We are proud of our happy and friendly school in which staff, governors, children and parents work hard to provide the best possible start to school life. Our entire school community works to develop our ‘MIRROR’ learning values in our children. We are proud of how everyone works together as a team to reinforce and implement the aims of our school.
A school will only achieve its full potential if we all work together as a team. By teaching the importance of the experience of school and supporting our children to value their education and learning, we enable them to establish skills and strategies to become life-long learners. At Vigo, we encourage every child’s sense of self-worth and develop their capacity to live as an independent, self-motivated person who respects and values themselves and all others.
Our curriculum ensures that we teach an engaging, broad and balanced curriculum that is driven by key big questions and concepts like diversity, equality, friendship and democracy. Through our curriculum and our pastoral curriculum, your child will be involved in experiencing school life to the full, developing not only the academic potential of your child but the social and moral sides of their character too.
We are lucky to have large grounds where our children can play and explore. We deliver Forest School sessions across the year and even have a school dog, Ralph, who our children can take for a walk.
Our website is a window into our school. Please take the time to navigate the pages. To gain the best view of our school, please arrange a visit - there is more to Vigo than you think!

Curriculum
In line with our inclusive ethos, we have developed a curriculum that ensures all learners can access and succeed. Our curriculum offer ensures that throughout the primary phases, the progression of knowledge and skills is carefully mapped to support strong pupil outcomes.
Our curriculum is designed to enable our experienced teachers to plan engaging and inspiring learning opportunities that prepare our children for their next steps in learning. We want all of our children to develop a learner profile that is Motivated, Independent, Resilient, Responsible, Open-minded and Respectful. We aspire to create lifelong learners who are well prepared for life after Vigo.
Below you will find our foundation curriculum; please enjoy taking some time to read through the exciting and progressive curriculum on offer at Vigo Primary School for each year group. Subsequently, each curriculum area has a dedicated page where you can read subject specific documentation.
If you would like further information regarding our curriculum or you would like hard copies of any documentation, please contact the school office or speak to your child's class teacher.
At Vigo primary school, we ensure that our curriculum is accessible to all learners. In the event that the learning journey of a child requires reasonable adjustments or adaptions, then the school's SENCo will work with the class teacher to develop an individual learning plan that will meet the needs of the learner and be fully inclusive of the curriculum. All adaptions will be in consultation with parents and further information can be found on the Inclusion pages of the school website.
